note: Cursor subagent identifiers for every executor launched against this run, recorded at launch time. The set of executors requested is therefore independent of the set that answered, and the broker's own per-task worker_id (see evidence/summary.json, tasks.by_executor) says which of them actually did each piece of work.
host_constraint: The agent host caps concurrent subagent sessions at 10. One hundred ranks are therefore served by roughly ten executors under oversubscription, exactly as `mpirun -np 100` runs a hundred ranks on eight cores. A rank is a durable role whose state lives outside its executor, which is what makes this legal; it works only because the protocol is in the harness, since an executor serving ten ranks agent-side would have to be inside ten barriers at once.

waves.assignment: round-robin, executor e serves ranks {r : r mod 10 == e}

waves.why: The first wave's executors reach their task limit and exit while work remains. Because the broker is a pull queue rather than a push, a fresh wave can be added mid-run against exactly the ranks that still have queued work, with no change to the harness and no restart. That elasticity is the reason the queue is a pull.
Two agents launched against an earlier attempt at this run before it was reconfigured; they are recorded because their worker ids appear in the journal.

quorum_note: The glossary allreduce carried a quorum of 0.9 and released when 93 of 100 ranks had contributed, rather than waiting for seven whose executor had not yet been started. This is the mechanism working as specified: reaching quorum releases the collective but does not close it, so the late ranks still pass through and still read the arbitrated glossary.
